about.title: Every crown starts with a precise fit
body: Crown Dental was built around a simple idea: restorative dentistry — crowns, bridges, implants — succeeds or fails on precision, not just skill in the chair. Every case here starts with careful diagnosis and ends with a fit that's checked, not assumed.

Led by Dr. V. Sangeetha, our multispeciality team covers restorative, cosmetic, and orthodontic care under one roof in Mugalivakkam, so patients don't need to bounce between clinics for connected treatment.

services.name: Dental Crowns & Bridges
services.tagline: A precise fit for lasting restorations
services.overview: Our core speciality — crowns and bridges fabricated and fitted with careful measurement and lab coordination, so restorations sit right the first time and hold up for years.
symptoms: Missing tooth affecting bite or appearance
procedure: Temporary crown while lab fabricates final restoration
benefits: Choice of ceramic, zirconia, or metal-ceramic crowns
services.recovery: Most patients resume normal eating within a day of final placement; minor sensitivity settles within a week.

faqs.question: How long does a crown take from start to finish?
faqs.answer: Typically two visits over 5–7 days — one for preparation and impressions, one for final fitting, with a temporary crown in between.

services.name: Root Canal Treatment
services.tagline: Save the natural tooth, relieve the pain
services.overview: Root canal therapy to treat infected or badly decayed teeth, typically followed by a crown to protect and restore the tooth long-term.
symptoms: Sensitivity to hot or cold that lingers
Swelling or tenderness near a tooth
procedure: Diagnosis with clinical exam and X-ray
Removal of infected pulp under local anaesthesia
Cleaning and sealing of the root canal
Crown placement to protect the treated tooth
benefits: Saves the natural tooth instead of extraction
Relieves pain from infection or decay
services.recovery: Mild soreness for 2–3 days is normal; a follow-up crown is typically placed within two weeks.

services.name: Dental Implants
services.tagline: A permanent replacement for missing teeth
services.overview: Titanium implants placed to replace missing teeth, topped with a custom-fitted crown for a result that looks and functions like a natural tooth.
procedure: Custom crown fitted onto the implant
benefits: Functions and feels like a natural tooth
services.recovery: Initial healing takes 1–2 weeks; full osseointegration before crown placement typically takes 8–12 weeks.

services.name: Braces & Orthodontics
services.overview: Orthodontic treatment for children and adults, including traditional braces and clear aligners, led by our in-house orthodontist.
benefits: Options for both children and adults
Coordinated with restorative care when needed
Improves bite function, not just appearance
services.recovery: Mild discomfort for a few days after each adjustment is normal and settles quickly.

services.name: Full Mouth Rehabilitation
services.overview: A coordinated treatment plan combining crowns, implants, and other restorative work to rebuild function and appearance across the whole mouth.
symptoms: Extensive wear from grinding or age
procedure: Coordinated crown, bridge, and implant work
benefits: Single coordinated plan instead of piecemeal fixes
services.recovery: Treatment is phased over several weeks to months depending on case complexity.

services.name: Teeth Whitening
services.tagline: A brighter smile in a single visit
services.overview: In-clinic professional whitening for patients looking to brighten their smile safely and evenly, without damaging enamel.
symptoms: Staining from coffee, tea, or tobacco
benefits: Visible results in a single session
Professionally supervised, safer than store kits
services.recovery: Mild sensitivity for a day or two is common and resolves on its own.

blogPosts.title: Crowns vs. Fillings: When Do You Actually Need a Crown?
blogPosts.excerpt: Not every cavity needs a crown, but some do. Here's how we decide, and why the difference matters for how long the repair lasts.
blogPosts.author: Dr. V. Sangeetha
content: Fillings work well for small to moderate cavities where enough healthy tooth structure remains to support the repair. They're quicker, cheaper, and less invasive.
Crowns come in when the damage is more extensive — a large cavity, a cracked tooth, or a tooth that's already had a root canal and needs protection from further fracture.
The general rule we use: if more than half the visible tooth structure is compromised, a filling is unlikely to hold up long-term and a crown is the more durable choice.

The trade-off is time and cost — a crown typically needs two visits and lab fabrication, versus a same-visit filling. But for the right case, it prevents repeat trips back to the chair for the same tooth.
If you're unsure which applies to you, an exam and X-ray usually settles it quickly — we'll always explain the reasoning before recommending either option.
